name: Choose the pro-verb after a pronoun in a comparison (as she does)
description: At the end of a comparison or elided clause it supplies the pro-verb that matches the subject ("twice as much as she does", "the South Pole always is", "Everyone does", or just the period when the verb is understood). Ablated, the model prefers "has", "a", "no", "are" or a comma.
